source_identity.paper: Xiaofan Bai et al., SkillZip: Evaluation-Free Skill Compression for Self-Evolving Agents by Discovering Reusable Structure

primary_claims_audited: One-shot SkillZip compresses evolved skills by 27.1-36.9% (31.2% average) while macro-average task score is reported as 0.577 versus 0.570 for the uncompressed evolved skill across the tested nine model-benchmark cells.

In a 16-round LiveMath SkillOpt self-evolution loop on three backbones, Zip-on-Write from round 1 is reported to keep endpoint skill length near 1.6x-1.9x seed instead of about 2.5x-3.7x without compression, a reported 38-50% endpoint reduction.

The reported final held-out accuracies for no-compression / Zip-on-Write@8 / Zip-on-Write@1 are 0.395/0.399/0.409 for Qwen3.6-Plus, 0.476/0.471/0.488 for Qwen3.7-Max, and 0.438/0.429/0.441 for Kimi-K2.6.
The structural compressor operates on already accepted evolution patches; it is a representation/consolidation mechanism, not the behavioral promotion gate.
published_claim_scope.scope_guard: The audit concerns the released SkillZip compression implementation and the specific reported one-shot/16-round LiveMath experiments. It does not establish universal behavioral equivalence, parser completeness, or the validity of SkillOpt's behavioral acceptance decisions.

official_artifact.judgment: The official release strongly supports inspection and reuse of the compression mechanism itself, including one-shot and Zip-on-Write semantics on caller-supplied accepted patches. The public release does not, from the files/branches/releases located in this audit, provide the proposal/acceptance chronology and orchestration required to reconstruct the paper's full 16-round SkillOpt LiveMath experiment or its headline numerical endpoints.

independent_artifact.relationship_note: This separate-account non-fork repository was created before the currently observed official GitHub repository creation timestamp. That chronology is consistent with an independent paper-based reimplementation but does not by itself prove organizational independence.
independent_artifact.implementation_scope: JavaScript reimplementation of the paper's typed-contract extraction, MDL-style optimization, workflow reuse, coverage constraint, structural audit and Zip-on-Write operations, with a committed LiveMath appendix fixture and unit/integration test runner.
independent_artifact.declared_fixture_result: README reports deterministic-mode compression of the Appendix C.E LiveMath fixture from 870 to 752 estimated tokens (13.6%), while noting the paper's 936 to 638 (32%) result uses LLM semantic relation judgments not reproduced by the deterministic-only fixture path.
independent_artifact.test_contract_inspected: test/run-tests.mjs asserts stable scanning, typed extraction, repeated-rule merging, coverage, deterministic rendering, >=10% compression with audit pass, ABSORB/EXTEND/REFINE Zip-on-Write behavior, repacking and approximate idempotence.
independent_artifact.interpretation: This is useful mechanism-level independent implementation evidence and a narrower fixture-level numerical comparison. The lower deterministic compression figure is not a failed replication of the paper's headline because the implementation/mode and token estimator differ and the community README explicitly scopes the comparison.

public_search_result.third_party_reviews_or_summaries: Found, but not treated as replication because they restate/analyze primary-study numbers rather than independently rerun the experiment.

reproducibility_assessment.official_artifact_support: strong for mechanism semantics; incomplete for paper-level experiment replay
reproducibility_assessment.independent_replication: partial mechanism reimplementation plus fixture-level deterministic compression only
reproducibility_assessment.judgment: SkillZip has materially stronger support than paper-only evidence: the official compressor is public and inspectable, and a separate non-fork implementation independently reconstructs the major algorithmic pieces and tests a paper-derived LiveMath fixture. However, the main 31.2% one-shot aggregate and 16-round 38-50% growth-control/final-accuracy results remain primary-study numerical evidence because the public author release does not expose the fixed accepted-patch chronology, SkillOpt orchestration, raw per-round trajectory/result bundle or final-test replay needed for an exact rerun, and no independent end-to-end rerun was found.
exact_blockers: Official GitHub release exposes the compressor API/library but not an end-to-end SkillOpt/LiveMath 16-round experiment driver or accepted-patch sequence.

No raw Figure-5/16-round trajectory table, per-round patch chronology, seeds/model-call replay bundle, or final-test invocation bundle was located in the official repository branch/release surface inspected.
The model-assisted path is OpenAI-compatible and runtime-configured; repository state alone does not freeze provider/model service behavior for the paper's model-assisted runs.

The independent JavaScript implementation provides mechanism tests and a deterministic fixture result, not an exact reproduction of the paper's LLM-assisted 31.2% aggregate or 16-round self-evolution endpoints.
No independent public numerical rerun of the full paper experiment was identified in the targeted search.
This audit did not execute the repositories locally; its conclusions are artifact/provenance inspection plus public-search evidence, not a new numerical rerun.
reproducibility_assessment.downstream_use: Evidence comparator/integrator may use this audit only for arxiv:2608.11079v2 source-matched candidates and only to classify artifact support/reproduction status. Do not attach it to a different paper or to a bare short candidate id. Do not upgrade the reported paper numbers to independently replicated.

exact_next_action: Search author-controlled project pages/arXiv ancillary material and repository history for the exact 16-round LiveMath SkillOpt accepted-patch sequence, model/seed invocation manifest and final-test replay bundle. If those remain absent, audit the next high-value C11 source with executable artifacts rather than simulating a different proposer or treating community mechanism tests as the missing end-to-end replication.
